'''Luka Šamanić''' (born 9 January 2000) is a Croatian professional [[basketball]] player for [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]]. A [[power forward]], he was drafted 19th overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Beer|title=An Early 2019 NBA Mock Draft: Duke's Barrett And Reddish On Track To Go 1-2|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tommybeer/2018/09/12/early-2019-nba-mock-draft/#6cb734f819eb|work=[[Forbes]]|date=12 September 2018|access-date=21 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=NBA draft scouting: 10 international prospects for 2019 and beyond|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/24324900/nba-draft-scouting-luka-samanic-fiba-u18-european-championships|work=[[ESPN]]|date=9 August 2018|access-date=21 September 2018}}</ref>

A native of [[Zagreb]], Šamanić started his youth career with the [[KK Zagreb|eponymous basketball club]]. In 2016, at age 16, he moved to [[Barcelona]], Spain, where he joined the [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]]'s [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet B|reserve team]] in the Spanish [[LEB Oro|second-tier league]]. Šamanić has represented [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatia]] multiple times in [[FIBA]] events, leading his team to a [[gold medal]] at the [[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship#Division B|FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]] in 2017, while earning [[most valuable player]] honors.

==Early life==
Šamanić was born in [[Zagreb]], Croatia.<ref name="scouting">{{cite web |last1=Gaibotti |first1=Federico |title=Luka Samanic, scouting report about the rising Croatian prospect |url=https://www.basketuniverso.it/luka-samanic-scouting-report-about-the-rising-croatian-prospect/ |publisher=BasketUniverso |access-date=31 August 2018 |date=22 January 2018}}</ref> His father, Marko Šamanić, played basketball professionally for 19 years, including in the [[EuroLeague]], with Slovenian club [[KK Krka|Krka]].<ref name="development">{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Development is priority for Barcelona talent Samanic |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8gke7iov3ioav8uo/development-is-priority-for-barcelona-talent-samanic |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=31 August 2018 |date=10 January 2018}}</ref> Due to his father's career, Šamanić lived in a number of countries in his early life. When he was nine months old, he moved to Belgium, and he later stayed in Slovenia and Germany.<ref name="globetrotter">{{cite web |title=Globe-trotter, late starter Samanic out to follow in stars' footsteps |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2016/news/globe-trotter-late-starter-samanic-out-to-follow-in-stars-footsteps |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=3 September 2018 |date=11 August 2016}}</ref>

Šamanić grew up playing a variety of sports, including [[association football|football]], [[handball]], [[tennis]], and was also involved in [[breakdancing]].<ref name="eurocamp2">{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Schmitz |first2=Mike |title=2016 Adidas EuroCamp: Day Two |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2016-adidas-Eurocamp-Day-Two-5555/ |publisher=DraftExpress |access-date=1 September 2018 |date=11 June 2016 |archive-date=13 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613214459/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2016-adidas-Eurocamp-Day-Two-5555/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="talented">{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Talented trio Pecarski, Garuba, Samanic leading the way at U16 Euros |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/news/talented-trio-pecarski-garuba-samanic-leading-the-way-at-u16-euros |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=31 August 2018 |date=18 August 2016}}</ref> He did not start playing basketball, the last sport he attempted, until he was 11 years old.<ref name=talented/> He credits his football experience for improving his coordination as a basketball player.<ref name=globetrotter/>

==Youth career==
Šamanić began his basketball career at the youth levels with local club [[KK Zagreb|Zagreb]].<ref name="defensive">{{cite web |title=Defensive ace Luka Samanic voted MVP, headlines All-Star Five team |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18b/2017/news/defensive-ace-luka-samanic-voted-mvp-headlines-all-star-five-team |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=31 August 2018 |date=6 August 2017}}</ref> He collected 29 points, 10 rebounds, 4 steals, and 3 blocks for Zagreb in a 22 November 2014 win over the junior team for Šanac Karlovac.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kadeti ponovo susped! |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=3949 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=31 August 2018 |language=hr |date=22 November 2014}}</ref> On 16 November, he recorded 43 points, 8 rebounds, and 7 steals for Zagreb to help defeat Samobor, 160–21.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kadeti postigli 160 koševa u novoj pobjedi! |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=5157 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=hr |date=16 November 2015}}</ref> On 3 January 2016, Šamanić led his team to a championship win against [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Virtus Roma]] in a youth tournament in Italy, for which he earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kadeti prvi u Italiji, Luka Šamanić MVP! |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=5334 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=hr |date=3 January 2016}}</ref> He scored 32 points on 16 January, in a blowout 111–43 win over the Rudeš junior team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nova pobjeda kadeta |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=5394 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=hr |date=16 January 2016}}</ref> Later in the month, Šamanić dominated versus the [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]] junior team, notching 26 points, 10 rebounds, 4 steals, and 4 blocks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kadeti uvjerljivi protiv Cedevite |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=5500 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=hr |date=25 January 2016}}</ref> He continued his success on 22 February, when he erupted for 39 points and 21 rebounds in a 160–50 win over the junior team for Sisak.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kadeti protiv Siska slavili sa 110 razlike |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=5656 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=hr |date=22 February 2016}}</ref> On 29 May, Šamanić was named MVP of the Croatian cadet championship after his [[double (basketball)|double-double]] of 16 points and 11 rebounds in a blowout of [[KK Cibona|Cibona]] junior squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kadeti Zagreba prvaci Hrvatske! |url=http://www.kk-zagreb.hr/?p=6073 |publisher=[[KK Zagreb]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=hr |date=29 May 2016}}</ref> In June, he attended the [[Adidas]] EuroCamp, a three-day pre-[[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) [[NBA draft|draft]] camp for international prospects held in [[Treviso]], Italy.<ref name=eurocamp2/><ref>{{cite web |title=adidas Eurocamp Announces 2016 Player Roster |url=https://news.adidas.com/us/Latest-News/adidas-eurocamp-announces-2016-player-roster/s/1689ad8b-ec1e-43c0-ab56-d42aad370b68 |publisher=[[Adidas]] |access-date=15 September 2016 |date=8 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922024545/https://news.adidas.com/us/Latest-News/adidas-eurocamp-announces-2016-player-roster/s/1689ad8b-ec1e-43c0-ab56-d42aad370b68 |archive-date=22 September 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 14 June 2016, Šamanić signed a 2-year amateur contract with Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]], initially joining its junior ranks.<ref name=eurocamp2/><ref>{{cite web |title=Luka Samanic, al Barça: croata de 15 años y 2.08 m. Así juega la sensación en Treviso |url=http://www.gigantes.com/cantera/luka-samanic-al-barca-croata-de-15-anos-y-2-08-m-asi-juega-la-sensacion-en-treviso-video/ |publisher=Gigantes del Basket |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=es |date=14 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=El Barça Lassa B ya trabaja en la Ciutat Esportiva |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.es/secciones/baloncesto/fc-barcelona-b/noticias/2016-2017/el-barca-lassa-b-ya-trabaja-en-la-ciudad-esportiva |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=3 September 2018 |language=es |date=17 August 2016}}</ref> On 22 December, he won the [[slam dunk|Slam Dunk]] Contest at a youth tournament in [[Tenerife]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Así se llevó Luka Samanic el concurso de mates del Torneo Junior Tenerife |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=128235 |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |language=es |date=22 December 2016 |archive-date=20 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620013745/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=128235 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In January 2017, Šamanić played with Barcelona's junior team at the Ciutat By August 2017, Šamanić was drawing attention from several [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=FIBA u18: College an option for Luka Samanic |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/FIBA-u18-College-an-option-for-Croatia-native-Luka-Samanic--105712290/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=21 September 2018 |date=2 August 2017}}</ref> In the 2017–18 season with Barcelona's junior team, he assumed a greater role after many of its top players left.<ref name=development/> In January 2018, Šamanić joined Barcelona at the Ciutat de L'Hospitalet qualifiers for the [[2017–18 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2017–18 Adidas Next Generation Tournament]].<ref name=realgm/> He posted 27 points, 16 rebounds, and 3 blocks on 7 January, as his team lost to the [[Club Joventut Badalona|Joventut Badalona]] junior team in the championship.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stankovic |first1=Vladimir |title=Los 10 cracks del Torneo de L'Hospitalet |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/20180108/434169465795/samanic-lidera-una-buena-cosecha.html |website=[[Mundo Deportivo]] |access-date=21 September 2018 |language=es |date=8 January 2018}}</ref> Still, Šamanić was named L'Hospitalet tournament MVP and earned All-Tournament Team honors after averaging 23.2 points, 14.8 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2.8 blocks through 4 games.<ref name=realgm/><ref>{{cite web |title=Barcelona's Samanic named ANGT L'Hospitalet MVP |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8gdb4omnc5us683e/barcelona-s-samanic-named-angt-l-hospitalet-mvp |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=21 September 2018 |date=7 January 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===FC Barcelona B (2017–2018)===
In the [[2017–18 LEB Oro season|2017–18 season]], Šamanić competed for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet B]]—the [[reserve team]] of FC Barcelona—in the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]], the [[Spanish basketball league system|second-tier Spanish league]].<ref name="realgm2">{{cite web |title=Luka Samanic Game Logs |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Luka-Samanic/GameLogs/94639/International/2018/55 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> He debuted on 1 October 2017, in a 76–69 win over [[Força Lleida CE|Força Lleida]], playing only 4 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oct 1, 2017: Actel Forca Lleida 69, FC Barcelona II 76 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-10-01/Actel-Forca-Lleida-at-FC-Barcelona-II/271930 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=15 September 2018 |date=1 October 2017}}</ref> Šamanić stood out in his next game versus [[Cáceres Ciudad del Baloncesto|Cáceres]], scoring 10 points in 20 minutes and performing a [[slam dunk#Windmill|windmill dunk]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fernández |first1=Marcos |title=El blaugrana Luka Samanic da espectáculo en LEB: matazo 'molinillo' ante Cáceres |url=http://www.gigantes.com/cantera/jovenes-promesas/el-blaugrana-luka-samanic-da-espectaculo-en-leb-matazo-molinillo-ante-caceres-video/ |publisher=Gigantes del Basket |access-date=15 September 2018 |language=es |date=7 October 2017}}</ref> On 4 November 2017, he scored 11 points in 19 minutes against [[Araberri BC|Araberri]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nov 4, 2017: FC Barcelona II 68, Saenz Horeca Araberri |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-11-04/FC-Barcelona-II-at-Saenz-Horeca-Araberri/288316 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=15 September 2018 |date=4 November 2017}}</ref> In his following appearance, Šamanić collected 10 points and 8 rebounds in a win over [[CB Peñas Huesca|Peñas Huesca]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fernández |first1=Marcos |title=Competiciones FEB en clave Junior (8). Mira los Sub-20 más destacados de la semana |url=http://www.gigantes.com/cantera/competiciones-torneos-y-campeonatos/competiciones-feb-clave-junior-8-mira-los-sub-20-mas-destacados-la-semana/ |publisher=Gigantes del Basket |access-date=15 September 2018 |language=es |date=20 November 2017}}</ref> He scored a season-high 17 points on 9 February 2018, leading his team past [[Palencia Baloncesto|Palencia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Feb 9, 2018: FC Barcelona II 64, Quesos Cerrato de Palencia 62 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-02-09/FC-Barcelona-II-at-Quesos-Cerrato-de-Palencia/294569 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=15 September 2018 |date=9 February 2018}}</ref> Through 22 games, Šamanić averaged 5.1 points, 2 rebounds, and 0.7 assists in 12.7 minutes per game.<ref name=realgm/> In February 2018, he took part in a [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp in [[Los Angeles]], joining several other international NBA prospects.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Basketball Without Borders: Camp preview and full roster reveal |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22360171/2018-basketball-borders-preview-full-rosters-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=21 September 2018 |date=8 February 2018}}</ref>

===Olimpija (2018–2019)===
On 31 May 2018, Šamanić signed a multi-year professional contract with [[KK Olimpija|Petrol Olimpija]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian League]] and [[ABA League]].<ref name="olimpija">{{cite web |title=Luka Šamanić prva okrepitev po koncu sezone |url=http://www.petrol.olimpija.com/novice/luka-amanic-prva-okrepitev-po-koncu-sezone |publisher=[[KK Olimpija]] |access-date=10 September 2018 |language=sl |date=31 May 2018 |archive-date=24 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624112712/http://www.petrol.olimpija.com/novice/luka-amanic-prva-okrepitev-po-koncu-sezone |url-status=dead }}</ref> He joined Olimpija after failing to agree to terms with Croatian club [[KK Zadar|Zadar]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Šamanić napustio Barcelonu |url=https://basketball.hr/vijesti/video-samanic-napustio-barcelonu/5232 |publisher=Basketball.hr |access-date=10 September 2018 |language=hr |date=22 May 2018}}</ref> Šamanić debuted for Olimpija on 21 September in an 86–60 loss to [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] at the [[2018 ABA League Supercup]], recording 2 points and 3 rebounds in 19 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |title=CZV - OLI |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/match.php?id=4&sez=18&lea=3&tab=Boxscore&q=q1 |publisher=[[ABA League]] |access-date=22 September 2018 |date=21 September 2018}}</ref> On 7 May 2019, he recorded season-high marks of 22 points and 11 rebounds in an 85–73 win over [[KK Šenčur|Šenčur]] in the Slovenian League.<ref>{{cite web |title=May 7, 2019 - Sencur Gorenjska Gradbena Druzba Kranj 73 at Union Olimpija 85 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-05-07/Sencur-Gorenjska-Gradbena-Druzba-Kranj-at-Union-Olimpija/334007 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=16 May 2019 |date=7 May 2019}}</ref> In late June 2019, [[KK Olimpija|Petrol Olimpija]] announced the departure of Šamanić.<ref>{{cite web|title=Luka Šamanić bo kariero nadaljeval v Ligi NBA|language=sl|url=http://www.petrol.olimpija.com/novice/luka-amanic-bo-kariero-nadaljeval-v-ligi-nba|date=27 June 2019|website=olimpija.com|access-date=27 June 2019|archive-date=30 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630152003/http://www.petrol.olimpija.com/novice/luka-amanic-bo-kariero-nadaljeval-v-ligi-nba|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Luka Šamanić leaves Olimpija to join San Antonio Spurs |url=https://druga.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=42055 |website=aba-liga.com |access-date=29 June 2019}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2019–2021)===
On 20 April 2019, Šamanić declared his entry into the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/DraftExpress/status/1119633495117185026|title=6'11 Croatian forward Luka Samanic has entered the 2019 NBA draft, a source told ESPN. The 19-year old is ranked #39 on the ESPN 100 and will likely get looks in the first round.|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|date=20 April 2019|website=Twitter.com|access-date=25 April 2019}}</ref> He became one of a record-high 58 international prospects to declare entry that year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=NBA draft: 233 early-entry prospects declare for 2019 |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26586762/nba-draft-233-early-entry-prospects-declare-2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=26 April 2019 |date=23 April 2019}}</ref> Šamanić later entered the 2019 [[NBA Draft Combine]] as one of 77 total participants.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/article/2019/05/08/66-players-attend-nba-draft-combine Sixty-six players expected to attend NBA Draft Combine]</ref> On 20 June 2019, Šamanić was the 19th pick of the [[2019 NBA draft]], after being selected by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 NBA Draft Grades: Pick-by-pick evaluations for every first- and second-round selection |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2019-nba-draft-grades-pick-by-pick-evaluations-for-every-first-and-second-round-selection/ |website=cbssports.com |access-date=21 June 2019}}</ref> On 1 July 2019, Šamanić officially signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web |title=SPURS SIGN 2019 FIRST ROUND PICK LUKA SAMANIC |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2019-first-round-pick-luka-samanic |website=NBA.com |access-date=1 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref> On 30 October 2019, Šamanić received his first assignment to the [[Austin Spurs]], the affiliate team of the San Antonio Spurs in [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=SPURS ASSIGN LUKA SAMANIC AND KELDON JOHNSON TO AUSTIN SPURS|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-assign-luka-samanic-and-keldon-johnson-austin-spurs|date=30 October 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=30 October 2019}}</ref>

On 13 August 2020, Šamanić recorded 16 points and 6 rebounds in a 112–118 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], on his first NBA game as a starter.

The Spurs waived Šamanić on 11 October 2021 as part of the final roster cuts before the [[2021–22 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs waive Luka Samanic |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-waive-luka-samanic |website=NBA.com |access-date=17 October 2021 |date=11 October 2021}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2021–2022)===
On 16 October 2021, Šamanić was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Luka Šamanić to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-luka-samanic-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=17 October 2021 |date=16 October 2021}}</ref> On 17 March 2022, he was waived without appearing in a game for New York.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Waive Luka Šamanić |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-waive-luka-samanic |website=NBA.com |access-date=18 March 2022 |date=17 March 2022}}</ref>

===Maine Celtics (2022–2023)===
On 22 September 2022, Šamanić signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtics' Luka Samanic: Inks training camp deal |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-luka-samanic-inks-training-camp-deal/amp/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=3 October 2022 |date=22 September 2022}}</ref> He was waived by the Celtics on 10 October.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtics Waive Luka Samanic, Sign A.J. Reeves |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/10/celtics-to-waive-luka-samanic-sign-a-j-reeves.html |website=Hoops Rumors |access-date=16 October 2022 |date=11 October 2022}}</ref> On 24 October 2022, Šamanić joined the [[Maine Celtics]] training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/maine-celtics-select-two-in-g-league-draft-announce-training-camp-roster/n-5892371|title=Maine Celtics Select Two in G League Draft, Announce Training Camp Roster|date=24 October 2022|access-date=24 October 2022}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2023–2024)===
On 28 March 2023, Šamanić signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Luka Šamanić to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-luka-samanic-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=28 March 2023|access-date=28 March 2023}}</ref> and on 7 April, he signed a multi-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Luka Šamanić to Multi-Year Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-luka-samanic-to-multi-year-deal|website=NBA.com|date=7 April 2023|access-date=8 April 2023}}</ref>

On 5 August 2024, Šamanić signed with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Luka Samanic Fenerbahçe Beko’da|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2024/8/luka-samanic-fenerbahce-beko-da|website=Fenerbahce.org|date=5 August 2024|access-date=5 August 2024|language=Turkish}}</ref>
On 10 September 2024, the club announced that Šamanić went home to [[Croatia]] for personal reasons, four days prior to the announcement. <ref>https://x.com/FBBasketbol/status/1833544521361011007</ref>
On 13 September 2024, [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] followed up with the announcement that the club has terminated the contract of the player, by mutual consent, while still holding the rights for him for the [[2024–25 Basketbol Süper Ligi]] season, thus ending his 40-day tenure with the club.<ref>https://x.com/FBBasketbol/status/1834629594176954714</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Fenerbahce part ways with Luka Samanic |url=https://basketnews.com/news-211619-fenerbahce-part-ways-with-luka-samanic.html |access-date=2024-09-14 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Cibona (2024)===
In December 2024, Šamanić signed with [[KK Cibona|Cibona]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[Premijer liga (Croatian basketball)|Croatian League]]. This is the first time he will professionally play in his home country. Šamanić signed an open contract meaning he can transfer to another club for a more lucrative contract in any moment.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.index.hr/sport/clanak/luka-samanic-presao-u-cibonu/2621343.aspx |title=Luka Šamanić prešao u Cibonu |publisher=[index.hr |accessdate=16 December 2024 |language=hr |date=4 December 2024}}</ref>

===Baskonia (2024–2025)===
On 30 December 2024 he signed 1+1 contract with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]] for the rest of the season. On 22 October 2025 Šamanić and his team terminated his contract due to personal reasons.{{fact|date=May 2026}}

==National team career==
Šamanić represents [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatia]] in [[FIBA]] competition. He made his national team debut at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] in [[Radom]], Poland.<ref name=globetrotter/> On 16 August 2016, Šamanić recorded 17 points, 15 rebounds, 5 assists, and 9 blocks in a 74–67 victory over Sweden.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aug 16, 2016: Sweden 67, Croatia 74 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2016-08-16/Sweden-at-Croatia/239424 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=4 September 2018 |date=16 August 2016}}</ref> In his final game at the event, he posted 24 points and 12 rebounds, shooting 4-of-9 from the three-point line, in a loss to [[Turkey men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Turkey]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Aug 20, 2016: Croatia 70, Turkey 77 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2016-08-20/Croatia-at-Turkey/239432 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=4 September 2018 |date=20 August 2016}}</ref> As Croatia finished in fourth place, Šamanić averaged 17.7 points, 10.4 rebounds, and 2.9 blocks per game, earning All-Star Five honors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba claims MVP award to lead All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2016/news/usman-garuba-claims-mvp-award-to-lead-all-star-five |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=4 September 2018 |date=21 August 2016}}</ref> In 2017, he played at the [[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship#Division B|FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]] in [[Tallinn]], Estonia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Players to Watch at the FIBA U18 European Championship 2017 Division B |url=http://www.heinnews.com/basketball/international-basketball/fiba-basketball/players-to-watch-at-the-fiba-u18-european-championship-2017-division-b/ |publisher=heinnews |access-date=20 September 2018 |date=28 July 2017}}</ref> Šamanić led Croatia to a [[gold medal]] after recording 21 points, 8 rebounds, 4 steals, and 3 blocks in an overtime win over Great Britain.<ref>{{cite web |title=Croatia take home gold after overtime drama, Estonia finish on the podium |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18b/2017/news/croatia-take-home-gold-after-overtime-drama-estonia-finish-on-the-podium |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=20 September 2018 |date=6 August 2017}}</ref> He was named tournament MVP and made the All-Star Five after averaging 13.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.8 steals, and 1.6 blocks per game.<ref name=defensive/> Šamanić took part in the [[2018 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] in [[Latvia]].<ref name="amid">{{cite web |title=Amid lofty expectations, Samanic has high hopes for Croatia |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2018/news/amid-lofty-expectations-samanic-has-high-hopes-for-croatia |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=4 September 2018 |date=31 July 2018}}</ref> On 3 August 2018, he notched 29 points, 10 rebounds, and 4 blocks, shooting 5-of-5 from the three-point line, to help defeat Ukraine.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aug 3, 2018: Ukraine 62, Croatia 85 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2018-08-03/Ukraine-at-Croatia/307700 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=20 September 2018 |date=3 August 2018}}</ref> Even though Šamanić averaged 17 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game in the tournament, Croatia finished in 11th place.<ref name=realgm/>

Even though being a free agent at the time, in November, 2024, Šamanić debuted for the senior national team. His first two games were against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] in the [[EuroBasket 2025 qualification#Group E 2|EuroBasket 2025 qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=REPREZENTACIJA Izbornik odredio dvanaestoricu za utakmicu s BiH |url=https://www.hks-cbf.hr/reprezentacije/2024/reprezentacija-izbornik-odredio-dvanaestoricu-za-utakmicu-s-bih/ |publisher=[[Croatian Basketball Federation]] |accessdate=16 December 2024 |date=21 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=REPREZENTACIJA: Vrijeme je za drugo poluvrijeme s BiH, Hezonja preuzeo kapetansku traku |url=https://www.hks-cbf.hr/reprezentacije/2024/reprezentacija-vrijeme-je-za-drugo-poluvrijeme-s-bih-hezonja-preuzeo-kapetansku-traku/ |publisher=[[Croatian Basketball Federation]] |accessdate=16 December 2024 |date=24 November 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Aside from Croatian, Šamanić speaks English and Spanish. Off of the basketball court, he likes to play football and [[table tennis]].<ref name=amid/>

Šamanić's basketball influences are former Croatian national player [[Toni Kukoč]]
and American player [[Kevin Durant]].<ref name=amid/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Sam |title=Toni Kukoc Always Delivered |url=http://history.bulls.com/toni-kukoc-always-delivered/ |publisher=[[Chicago Bulls]] |access-date=15 September 2018 |date=27 December 2017 |archive-date=22 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922024643/http://history.bulls.com/toni-kukoc-always-delivered/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Radičević |first1=Vlado |title=Hrvatski tinejdžer potpuno zaludio NBA skaute; ovako nešto dugo nije viđeno! |url=https://www.tportal.hr/sport/clanak/hrvatski-tinejdzer-potpuno-zaludio-nba-skaute-ovako-nesto-dugo-nije-videno-20180109 |publisher=tportal |access-date=21 September 2018 |language=hr |date=9 January 2018}}</ref>
